facts.raw_span: A 40-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain and constipation
continued to have amenorrhea and reported abdominal fullness and constipation
Point-of-care (POC) urine human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) test: negative
Ultrasonography: Confirmed live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks
A 40-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain and constipation
continued to have amenorrhea and reported abdominal fullness and constipation
Point-of-care (POC) urine human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) test: negative
Ultrasonography: Confirmed live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks

concepts.why: The patient presented with amenorrhea and a high serum hCG level, and ultrasonography confirmed a live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks.
The patient had a history of thyroid condition, undetectable thyroid-stimulating hormone, and was prescribed methimazole.
The patient presented with constipation and abdominal fullness.
The patient had a tender midline abdominal mass on physical examination.
The patient had a history of amenorrhea and was found to have a live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks.
The patient had a negative point-of-care urine hCG test despite being 24 weeks pregnant.

rationales.F01: Abdominal pain and constipation could be related to various conditions, including intrauterine pregnancy or constipation itself.
rationales.F02: Amenorrhea can be a sign of pregnancy, but also of other conditions such as hyperthyroidism.
rationales.F08: A tender midline abdominal mass could be related to pregnancy or an abdominal mass.
rationales.F09: A negative point-of-care urine hCG test could be a false negative, especially if the patient is actually pregnant.
rationales.F10: High serum hCG levels are indicative of pregnancy.
rationales.F11: Ultrasonography confirming a live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks strongly supports the diagnosis of intrauterine pregnancy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's 3-4 months of amenorrhea, high serum hCG level, and ultrasonography confirming a live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks strongly support this diagnosis, despite the initial false-negative hCG test.
